title: Quarter-wave HfO2/SiO2 stack with bounded perturbation refinement
scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave stack centered at approximately 10500 nm with HfO2/SiO2 alternation will produce high emissivity in the 8000-13000 nm band and low emissivity in the 3000-5000 nm band, and small thickness perturbations (±0.5%) around quarter-wave values can improve the dual-band contrast without abandoning the fundamental periodic structure.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics: quarter-wave stacks create stopbands where reflectance is high. For an emitter on an absorbing substrate, high absorptance (thus high emissivity by Kirchhoff's law) occurs outside the stopband. By centering the quarter-wave condition at the middle of the target high-emissivity band, the stopband should fall in the unwanted 3-5 μm region. HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the infrared, providing the index contrast needed for a strong stopband.
proposed_topology: air / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / si substrate (20 layers total, starting with HfO2 at air interface)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses with ±0.5% perturbation bounds around quarter-wave optical thickness at 10500 nm center wavelength
quadratic penalty weight for deviation from quarter-wave condition (fixed at 0.05)
soft_objectives: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band
minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band
maintain layer thicknesses within ±0.5% of quarter-wave values to test the periodic foundation hypothesis
manufacturing_considerations: 20 layers is within the 24-layer maximum constraint
thicknesses in the 400-900 nm range are compatible with standard thin-film deposition
quarter-wave foundation provides a reproducible starting point for manufacturing
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high-reflectance stopbands centered at the design wavelength
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the infrared range, providing index contrast for interference effects
Recalled knowledge: Kirchhoff's law relates emissivity to absorptance for opaque substrates at thermal equilibrium
Recalled knowledge: Small perturbations around optimal periodic structures can sometimes improve bandwidth or sideband suppression without losing the fundamental interference mechanism
expected_advantages: Quarter-wave foundation provides physical interpretability of the design
Bounded perturbation keeps the optimization near a known-good region
20 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom while staying under the 24-layer limit
Periodic structure may be more robust to manufacturing thickness variations than fully aperiodic designs
known_risks: Uncertain whether quarter-wave center at 10500 nm is optimal -- the actual optimal center wavelength depends on the exact refractive indices of HfO2 and SiO2 at these wavelengths, which I am recalling approximately
Uncertain whether 20 layers is the optimal count -- more layers might improve contrast but approach the 24-layer limit; fewer might be insufficient
The ±0.5% perturbation bound might be too restrictive if the true optimum requires larger deviations from quarter-wave
Refractive index values in the 8-13 μm range for HfO2 and SiO2 are recalled from general knowledge; actual measured data may differ
What would settle these uncertainties: lookup of measured n/k data for HfO2 and SiO2 in the 3-13 μm range, and a sweep of layer counts from 10 to 24
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer planar multilayer dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat) (starting from air side). Optimize individual layer thicknesses with initial values at quarter-wave optical thickness for 10500 nm center wavelength, allowing ±0.5% perturbation from quarter-wave values. Apply quadratic penalty term with weight 0.05 for deviations from exact quarter-wave optical thickness. Target: maximize emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band, minimize emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band. Use materials hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), and si substrate. Total layer count fixed at 20.
revision_reason: Localized refinement round using top-scoring candidates from prior batch, applying 0.5% perturbation amplitude around quarter-wave thickness values with quadratic penalty (weight=0.05) for deviations from quarter-wave optical thickness. This tests whether the hypothesized periodic geometry closes the remaining performance gap or confirms the current asymmetric optimum is globally superior.
